t: Find the error: "Nothing but the marvellous buildings have the charm."
e: Real subject is 'Nothing', which is singular → "has the charm".

t: Find the error: "Each participant have performed well."
e: 'Each' always takes singular verb → "has performed well".

t: Find the error: "Aman and Karan has done well."
e: Two different subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb → "have done well".

t: Find the error: "There is two cats in the room."
e: With dummy subject 'there', the verb agrees with the real noun that follows → "There are two cats".

t: Find the error: "More than one boys were absent."
e: 'More than one' takes a singular noun and verb → "More than one boy was absent".

t: Find the error: "Bread and butter are a healthy breakfast."
e: 'Bread and butter' is a single idea → "is a healthy breakfast".

t: Find the error: "Mumps cause weak bones in children."
e: Diseases like mumps/measles/rickets take singular verb → "Mumps causes".

t: Find the error: "Five thousand rupees was spent on food and clothes separately."
e: When an amount is divided/spent separately, the verb becomes plural → "were spent".

t: Find the error: "A sharp fall in the price of jute have led to losses."
o: A sharp fall in the price of jute
e: The real subject is 'A sharp fall' (singular), not 'jute' → "has led".

t: Find the error: "Neither the manager nor the employees has noticed."
o: Neither the manager nor the employees
e: With 'neither...nor', verb agrees with the nearer subject 'employees' → "have noticed".

t: Find the error: "The principal, along with the vice principals, have approved."
o: The principal, along with the vice principals,
e: 'Along with' doesn't change the number of the subject; verb follows the first subject 'the principal' → "has approved".

t: Find the error: "Writing poems have been my hobby."
e: A gerund phrase as subject always takes a singular verb → "has been".

t: Find the error: "Around 30 percent of the Indian population are estimated to be literate."
o: Around 30 percent of the Indian population

t: Find the error: "Every boy, girl and teacher are present."
e: 'Every', even before multiple nouns, takes singular verb → "is present".

t: Find the error: "The jury is divided in their opinions."
e: When members of a collective noun disagree (divided), the verb is plural → "The jury are divided".
